newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta Energy expects C$300 mln gain.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Energy expects C$300 mln gain.

text.p: Alberta Energy Co Ltd said on Thursday its shareholders would realize C$300 million, or C$2.70 per share, from the restructuring of its pipeline division into a limited partnership.
AEC said net proceeds from the public offering of the pipeline assets, which have a market value of C$1.1 billion, would be used to reduce debt.

The company's 1996 yearend proforma debt-to-equity ratio would be 22:78 and the remaining C$670 million proforma long-term debt was sheltered against rising interest rates because 70 percent was fixed at 7.8 percent, it said.
Mandatory debt repayments for the next three years totalled C$4.5 million or one percent of 1996 cash flow, the company said. Its proforma cash flow interest coverage was pegged at 14.7 times.
AEC chief executive Gwyn Morgan said the limited partnership's C$1.1 billion value placed on the assets was far higher than as a wholly owned part of AEC.
The public offering was expected to close on April 9.

"This is approximately twice the value reflected in AEC's accounting statements, Morgan said in a statement. "Stock markets will now be in a much better position to reflect the value of the 70 percent of the AEC Pipelines Partnership retained by AEC in the price of the company's common shares."
AEC said its current C$700 million capital spending program included C$600 million in exploration and development.
Its drilling program targets 250 exploration and 200 development wells with the aim of growing sales this year by 18 percent on a barrel of oil equivalent basis.
